messages.subject: Diagnosing Problem of a Not Positive Definite Covariance Matrix
parts:
I'm stuck trying to find out why when I run my model with some data sets to compare factor means, I get an error saying the covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite in group 2, and with other data sets I get the error in groups 1 and 2, and with even other data sets, I don't get the error at all, even running the same model. Below is my syntax and output of the covariance matrices and the entire syntax and analysis comparing two groups' factor means (male/female) on eight factors. I have more complicated models that allow some error covariances and free some parameters to achieve metric invariance for a factor (ce), but I get the same error as this simpler model, so I thought I'd start with the simpler one. 

Thanks,
Brandon

messages.subject: Re: Diagnosing Problem of a Not Positive Definite Covariance Matrix
parts: I'm stuck trying to find out why when I run my model with some data sets to compare factor means, I get an error
It's a warning, not an error.

saying the covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite in group 2, and with other data sets I get the error in groups 1 and 2, and with even other data sets, I don't get the error at all, even running the same model.

Parameters are (assumed to be) constant, but estimates have sampling variability.  They vary across samples, and they can vary across models fit to the same data.
